## Hosted evidence

Two actual runs reach and pass both `Preview GitHub to pm plan` and `Gated GitHub to pm import`, then fail `Verify repeat import is a no-op` without publishing a branch:

- [PM Web run 45792469885 / job 139814702911](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/actions/runs/45792469885/job/139814702911), caller `12a277c0d4cb069af0c5b3ada73f08d02138f782`, installed pm-github `2026.11.25`. The repeat reports a changed `updated_at` on `pm-web-5sx6`. Consumer alert: [pm-web#369](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/issues/369).
- [PM RL run 45799801908 / job 139839761659](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/45799801908/job/139839761659), caller `273a68769d1ab37b1bbc89a71b4fba1a8f9613d6`. After the separate provenance issue was fixed by [pm-rl#211](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/pull/211), the repeat reports a changed `updated_at` on `pm-rl-github-eecd7460423f-202`. Consumer alert: [pm-rl#210](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/issues/210).

These are the same observed failure class, not proof of a single underlying cause. The logs do not show whether the provider records changed between the two imports, nor prove this is the same cause as the closed 2026.10.19 history-churn report #175. This is distinct from the host-compatibility, timestamp validation, and reserved-ID preview refusals.

## Acceptance

For a pinned unchanged source snapshot, the initial write and identical repeat must preserve the item timestamp, authoritative history and permitted changes on the repeat. If source inputs actually change between passes, return a clear source-drift diagnostic without publishing; retain the fail-closed privacy and no-op gates. Include a sanitized regression exercising both stable and changed evidence and verify the matching hosted workflow on at least one affected consumer.
Gated sync on 2026.11.25 stops at the repeat no-op check after item updated_at changes

value.text: Investigating the four hosted repeat-gate failures. The pinned caller reproduction will compare native documents and history across both passes and distinguish the published versions from the later merged comment fix.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Reproduced on pm-rl main e11861f with its locked PM CLI 2026.11.24 and pinned pm-github 2026.11.25. A frozen nine-issue REST and closure snapshot produced 17, 18, then 19 native comments for item 202. Both new comment_add rows share provider comment 7140375699. The repeat appended one history row touching comments and updated_at while reporting zero item updates and unchanged. Published 2026.11.26 differs in dist only by its version literal and predates merged #288. Auditing body, lifecycle, annotations, and dependency writes independently.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Release comparison confirmed: 2026.11.25 and 2026.11.26 both append comment 7140375699 twice (history 36 → 38 → 39). Merged #288 reads full native annotation text and preserves the original provider timestamp (history 36 → 38 → 38). Existing dependency writes are byte-idempotent on the pinned SDK but their duplicate receipt used to count a link. The workflow now compares a source-only snapshot before writes and still requires both byte-diff checks and the privacy scan. Consumer adoption and independent hosted verification are tracked in issue #297.

value.text: Review round 2. Merged the single upstream release commit. Checking the shared Projects association planners for many-to-one and one-to-many targets, including peers outside a selected scope. Checking reusable sync resolver, preview capability and caller guidance against a real older pin. Preview and apply must make the same pre-write decision.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Projects rule: each mutable plan target needs exactly one source. Audited import, pull, push, tags, wrapped issues, stale links, duplicate board rows and peer claims outside selected IDs. Every writable Projects association is checked before filtering for no-ops or executing a mutation. Pull cards without a resolved status remain inert. Issue import already rejects duplicate or conflicting source identities, refresh requires unique targets and closeout plans per item. Pin rule: a workflow hold selects an exact installed version and the workflow must explain and check its capability separately. The real 2026.11.26 package installs exactly and stops at gated preview with zero item/history writes. The sync diagnostic, input description, README, recovery guide and caller inventory all explain the source snapshot requirement and recovery. Closeout has a separate decision-code capability contract.

Removing only the shared board association check made seven adversarial cases fail: moved and contested pull, native import create and update, reassigned push with retained issue ownership, and peer claims during attachment and status writes. The uncontested control still passed. Removing the blocked preview branch restored the wrong pin diagnostic in a real CLI preview. value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Legacy-owner rule: a content writer must preserve accepted source authority and source kind across its proposed document. Native Projects import replaces descriptions, so it now omits that field when the shared parser finds a declaration that names the verified planned owner. The same decision drives preview and the no-op projection. Unrelated descriptions still refresh. Projects pull only writes lifecycle state and push only adds board provenance. Issue import and refresh preserve curated content or write the exact issue declaration and fidelity for a verified mirror. Export and closeout do not replace the native description. Both CLI receipt formats and packed consumers share the same command handler.
